text:
maya: Quick sync — we need a single invariant for quota/fallback errors before we flip the new routing UI. Goal: consistent status, a short human message for Console, and machine fields for SDKs/telemetry.

ravi: Agree. We keep seeing customers parse free-text and reagent clients retry incorrectly. What are the options? 429 vs 503 vs 409?

elaine: My take: use 429 for rate-limited quotas, 503 for capacity/scheduling fallback, and 409 for contract/version mismatches. Also include `retry_after` when known.

samir: +1 on semantics but we should add an explicit `fallback_type` machine field so SDKs can choose fallback model automatically. Something like: `fallback_type: "regional_fallthrough" | "downgrade_model" | "queue_delay"`.

maya: That would help. For Console UX we want to surface a friendly hint (one-liner) and an expandable diagnostics section that shows policy, region, and telemetry ids. But we must avoid leaking infra details to customers.

ravi: Right — diagnostics can be gated by org role. The public error shape could be: 
```json
{
  "status": 429,
  "error": "quota_exceeded",
  "message": "Quota exceeded for this key. Try again later or request higher quota.",
  "retry_after": 60,
  "machine_fields": {
    "error_class": "quota",
    "quota_name": "model_write_per_minute",
    "fallback_type": "downgrade_model",
    "telemetry_id": "tx-abc123"
  }
}
```
(we can inline the machine fields shape in docs, SDKs consume them).

elaine: Small ask: callers and telemetry pipelines prefer flatter keys rather than nested `machine_fields`. Maybe prefix `x_` fields at top level: `x_error_class`, `x_quota_name`, `x_fallback_type`, `x_telemetry_id`. Easier to index.

samir: Flattening is nice. Also include `x_routing_decision` with values `primary|fallback|queued` but redact node/region info unless org has enterprise role.

maya: Agreed on flattening. So canonical shape we propose: `status`, `error`, `message`, optional `retry_after`, and top-level `x_*` machine fields. Console will read `message` for one-liner and `x_telemetry_id` for link to traces.

ravi: One more: SDKs should map these to SDK-level error classes (QuotaError, CapacityFallback, TemporaryQueue) and expose `should_retry` boolean derived from status + `retry_after`. We should add a short spec in the SDK docs.

elaine: Ops/telemetry wants an invariant: all client-visible errors must include `x_error_class` and `x_telemetry_id`. If missing, reject during service validation. That will simplify metrics and alerts.

maya: Good. Can we also add a lightweight signal that says "was_routed_to_fallback": `x_routed=true|false`? Helpful for cost attribution.

samir: Fine, but make it boolean string to avoid type friction in older clients: `x_routed="true"`/"false". Documented.

ravi: Minor UX question: Console copy for 503 (fallback) should avoid saying "we downgraded your model" — customers panic. Use neutral language: "Reduced throughput to maintain availability; quality may vary." Expandable details for enterprise.

maya: Noted. We'll craft two SLO-aligned messages: public one-liner + admin detail.

deploy-bot: maya pushed config change to staging for error-shape validation (PR #4123) — deployment started. :rocket:

elaine: I'll add validation in the error-formatter middleware to enforce `x_error_class` and `x_telemetry_id`.

samir: I'll update SDK mapping patch to read `x_fallback_type` and set `should_retry` correctly.

maya: Plan: get staging validation green, update SDKs, then roll Console messaging in canary to 10% orgs next week. If no regressions, full rollout. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
